title: Gemini CLI Alternatives: What to Use Instead
summary: Gemini CLI alternatives after the June 18 change: which tools run Gemini models, how, what they cost, and how to move your GEMINI.md and MCP config.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Gemini CLI still runs for existing Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise organizations, Code Assist for GitHub on Google Cloud, and paid Gemini API or Vertex keys. Free accounts and Google AI Pro and Ultra lost it on June 18, 2026.
- Three of the nine tools after ours document all three Gemini routes (own plan, own key, Google Cloud): Antigravity CLI, OpenCode and Warp.
- Antigravity CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI read GEMINI.md as it is, Goose, Qwen Code, OpenCode and Warp load it after one setting or command, and the other three of the nine need a copy as AGENTS.md or their own rules file.
- Google's own-key price for Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon doubles on December 1, 2026, to $4 in and $20 out per million tokens, while the cheapest flat plans with a Gemini model cost $0 and $10 a month.


If you're comparing Gemini CLI alternatives, June 18, 2026 is probably why. That day Google stopped serving Gemini CLI requests for free personal accounts on Gemini Code Assist for individuals and for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. It pointed them to its new Antigravity CLI.


Gemini CLI itself is alive, open source under Apache 2.0, with v0.68.0 out on November 10. It now serves companies and paid keys, so this roundup of alternatives to Gemini CLI covers where to move, whether each tool runs Gemini, and what carries over. We pulled every price below on November 13, 2026.


We put[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) at the top because it's our product. The remaining nine are ranked by how many of three Gemini routes their own docs describe: Gemini billed through the tool's own plan, your own Gemini API key, and Vertex AI or other Google Cloud credentials. Ties go to the cheapest plan whose price includes Gemini use; tied tools without such a plan follow, alphabetically.


## Who can still run Gemini CLI after June 18


Gemini CLI wasn't switched off for everyone. Its README now opens with a status block that narrows who it's for, and Google's Code Assist sunset page, updated November 10, 2026, sets end dates for the enterprise route.


Who you are Can you still run Gemini CLI? What to know


Free personal Google account (Code Assist for individuals) No, since June 18, 2026 Moved to Antigravity CLI


Google AI Pro or Ultra subscriber No, since June 18, 2026 Moved to Antigravity CLI


Existing Code Assist Standard or Enterprise organization Yes, until the contract ends No new purchases since October 9, 2026; renewals end January 31, 2027 (annual) or December 31, 2027 (monthly); Gemini 3.x only


Gemini Enterprise subscription with a Code Assist entitlement Yes, until March 31, 2027 New Standard and Plus subscriptions no longer include it


Code Assist for GitHub through Google Cloud Yes Google says access is unchanged


Paid Gemini API or Vertex key Yes The README now calls these "legacy" keys


Anyone who wants Gemini 4 models Not tuned for them README: "Not optimized for Gemini 4+"


One case is missing on purpose: an unpaid Gemini API key. The README says "No free tier", while Google's older quota, plans and sign-in pages on geminicli.com still describe one, which is why year-old roundups call Gemini CLI free. Since Google's pages disagree, test your own key before you plan around it.


Even where access remains, the reasons to move add up. Gemini CLI isn't tuned for Gemini 4, and its own site banner sends Gemini 4 Argon users to Antigravity. The enterprise route has renewal deadlines, and paid-key prices rise on December 1 for Gemini 4 and on January 1 for 3.8 Flash.


On cutover day, a[Reddit thread in r/GeminiCLI](https://www.reddit.com/r/GeminiCLI/comments/1u93p4s/now_that_google_killed_gemini_cli_where_do_we/) asked where everyone was going. The top reply had switched to OpenCode and found it "much better", and another pointed to Antigravity CLI's automated migration. That's anecdotal, but both tools made our list. Firebase Studio, which shuts down on March 22, 2027, sends its users toward Antigravity as well, so plan any[Firebase Studio move](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/firebase-studio-alternatives) alongside this one.


## Gemini CLI alternatives compared by Gemini route


The last column answers what Gemini CLI users ask first: does the tool run Gemini, and how? The price column gives the free tier where one exists, then the lowest paid monthly plan.


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


Read that column as a route map: "in plan" means no Google bill of your own, and "own key" means paying Google per token at the prices further down.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** Switching agents without losing Google's models


**Overview:** Leaving Gemini CLI doesn't have to mean leaving Google's models. We run four coding agents, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode, on models from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI, as well as the open-source GLM and Kimi, all on one bill. You pick the agent for each job.


Each project has a cloud computer of its own, holding up to 1 TB, and the agents install software there, run it and publish it. They keep working when you step away, and several can run side by side, one chat apiece, on shared project files.


Some tasks need a person. On a separate Dedicated expert plan, a vetted developer takes the task from the same chat. We accept 0.82% of expert applicants, and a match can take as little as 24 hours.


**Key features:**


- Room for your own MCP servers beside 1,400+ app automations.
- A team keychain that everyone shares: once you add a key, teammates' agents can use it without seeing it.
- Scheduled recurring work that runs without a fresh prompt.
- Per-person model and budget limits for admins.


**Pricing:** Agentic plans charge each person a monthly price that doubles as their AI budget. Basic, where we'd start a Gemini CLI user, is $99, with Light at $19, Pro $199 and Studio $499, all with the same agents and models. They renew monthly with no refunds, and unspent budget doesn't roll over. The Dedicated expert plan is priced on a call and bundles one Light subscription.


For current Awesomic plans and capabilities, see[the pricing page](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


**Pros:** Google's models and three other makers' on one bill, side-by-side agent chats, a cloud computer that carries on without you, vetted developers through a separate expert plan


**Cons:** AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


**How to start using it:**


1. Go with Basic, or Light just to try the agents.
2. Create a project and connect GitHub.
3. Paste your GEMINI.md rules into the opening chat.
4. Hand one task to two agents in separate chats and compare.
5. If you need a developer more than agents, start on the Dedicated expert plan instead, which includes Light, and read the checkout total.


**Why it's a good Gemini CLI alternative:** Google's models stay on the menu without tying you to one vendor's agent.


**Final verdict:** Choose Awesomic for several agents and Google's models on one bill, plus a developer on a separate plan when agents stall. For a plain terminal agent with Gemini, Antigravity CLI (free, and it keeps your GEMINI.md) or OpenCode is the better pick.


To try the agents on your own repository,[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) on Basic.


### 2. Antigravity CLI


**Overview:** Antigravity CLI is the move Google built for Gemini CLI users, its Antigravity agents in a terminal under the` agy` command, and the one tool here with a full documented migration. On first launch it detects your configs, offers to convert them, and moves session tokens to your OS keyring.


Google's blog warned there "won't be 1:1 feature parity right out of the gate", though skills, hooks, subagents and extensions came across, the last as plugins. Unlike Gemini CLI, it's closed source, with no license on its public repo.


Migrators split on it in an[r/google_antigravity thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/google_antigravity/comments/1ur66xo/do_you_also_feel_that_gemini_cli_was_way_better/) on Reddit: one reply called it "a black box" and another "more effective overall", both anecdotal.


**Key features:**


- ` agy plugin import gemini` , turning extensions into plugins and old commands into skills.
- Background subagents managed with` /agents` .
- Your own Gemini key for CI runs, via` "modelProvider": "gemini"` plus` GEMINI_API_KEY` .


**Pricing:** The Individual tier costs $0 with a weekly quota on Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 3.8 Flash. Antigravity's page shows no prices for Pro or Ultra, but Google's subscriptions page lists Google AI Pro, adding Gemini 4 Argon, at $19.99 a month, and Ultra, adding Gemini 4 Carbon, at $99.99 or $199.99, sold as 5x and 20x Google AI Pro's usage limits.


**Pros:** A $0 tier, automatic conversion of your setup, Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon on paid tiers


**Cons:** Closed source, quota sizes unpublished and "subject to modification", no extra rate limits from your own key, Google's plans page and models table disagree on which tier gets Claude models


**What carries over:** Your context files, unedited, since Google's migration guide promises "identical workspace context rules".


**Final verdict:** Start here if you were on a free account or Google AI Pro, because it keeps your files and your Google sign-in.


### 3. OpenCode


**Overview:** OpenCode, an MIT-licensed agent for the terminal, desktop and IDE, is where that cutover-day Reddit reply landed. For Gemini users, the draw is choice: Gemini 4 Argon sits inside the $10 Go plan, your own key works through the` google` provider, and a single` google-vertex` provider covers Vertex with Application Default Credentials.


Context files take one extra step. OpenCode reads AGENTS.md, which its` /init` command creates, and falls back to CLAUDE.md. It doesn't name GEMINI.md, but listing the file under` instructions` in` opencode.json` loads it, so you don't need to copy it.


**Key features:**


- Sign-in with ChatGPT Plus or Pro, or with GitHub Copilot, in place of an API key.
- Free models, with a daily request limit.
- Desktop and mobile apps plus an SDK beside the terminal agent.


**Pricing:** The software is free, Go costs $10 a month with limits per five hours, week and month, and Go Plus is $40. Go's docs estimate 440 Gemini 4 Argon requests per five hours at a 50% discount that runs only through November 30, 2026.


**Pros:** Gemini 4 Argon in a $10 plan, open source under MIT, all three Gemini routes documented, sign-in with plans you may already have


**Cons:** GEMINI.md loads only once you list it in` opencode.json` , Go limits are estimates that vary by model, the Argon discount ends November 30, 2026


**Why it's a good Gemini CLI alternative:** You keep open-source code and gain a flat $10 monthly route to Gemini 4 Argon.


**Final verdict:** Choose OpenCode if you want open source and a cheap monthly plan with a Gemini 4 model in it.


### 4. Warp


**Overview:** Warp is a terminal with an agent built in, and the Warp Agent CLI brings that agent to any terminal through the` warp` command. Its homepage, captured above, now leads with Warp Factories, an early-access platform; we reviewed the terminal agent. The client code is open source under AGPL v3.


Warp's model list includes Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.1 Pro and several Gemini Flash versions. Personal bring-your-own-key covers Google models in local runs on Free and eligible paid plans, while your own Vertex AI account works on Enterprise only.


**Key features:**


- Project rules in AGENTS.md, with` /init` able to link an existing GEMINI.md.
- Hand-off from the CLI to Warp's cloud agents.
- Team-managed keys and endpoints, plus SAML SSO, on Business.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 with pay-as-you-go agent usage, and Build is $20 a month, or $18 a month billed annually, with $20 of usage at API rates included. Business is $50 per user a month, or $45 billed annually, for up to 25 seats.


**Pros:** All three Gemini routes, open client code, your own Google key on Free


**Cons:** Build's $20 is a usage budget at API rates, so heavy use costs more, Vertex routing needs Enterprise, a homepage that now sells Warp Factories ahead of the terminal


**Its edge for Gemini users:** You can start free on your own Google key and switch to built-in models later without changing tools.


**Final verdict:** Pick Warp if you want a new terminal and its agent in one, with Gemini through whichever route you already pay for.


### 5. Factory Droid


**Overview:** Droid is Factory's terminal agent, also offered as a desktop app and an SDK. Its models doc lists Gemini 4 Hydrogen at 0.6x, Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon at a promotional 0.8x, plus Gemini 3.1 Pro and several Flash versions, all billed through Factory's plan. Both Argon and Carbon return to 1.6x after December 1, 2026.


Your own Gemini key works too, through a generic chat-completion provider pointed at Google's API. Factory's docs add that only Anthropic and OpenAI models on their official APIs are "fully tested and benchmarked", so try a small task first.


**Key features:**


- AGENTS.md project rules, with CLAUDE.md among the compatible names.
- MCP servers added with` droid mcp add` .
- Autonomy levels and approval workflows.


**Pricing:** Free costs $0 when you bring your own inference through ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter or your own keys, and Pro costs $20 a month, with Plus at $100 and Max at $200. Teams costs $60 a month plus $40 per person, for up to 10 seats.


**Pros:** Gemini 4 models on discounted multipliers until December 1, a $0 tier on your own inference, approval controls


**Cons:** GEMINI.md isn't among its compatible filenames, own-key Gemini isn't fully tested, not open source, admin controls sit on Business rather than Teams


**Reason to shortlist it:** Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon sit inside a $20 plan, at a promotional 0.8x through December 1, 2026.


**Final verdict:** Choose Droid if you want Gemini 4 inside a $20 plan and approval controls over an autonomous agent, and budget for the 1.6x rate after December 1.


### 6. Goose


**Overview:** Goose is an Apache-2.0 agent from the Agentic AI Foundation that runs as a CLI, a desktop app and an API. It has no model plan, so Gemini comes through your own account: a Gemini provider that reads` GOOGLE_API_KEY` , or GCP Vertex AI, which serves both Gemini and Claude models.


Your GEMINI.md can stay as it is. Goose reads AGENTS.md and then .goosehints by default, and adding GEMINI.md to` CONTEXT_FILE_NAMES` makes it load yours as well.


**Key features:**


- Selectable thinking levels for Gemini 3 models.
- MCP extensions for work outside code.
- Context filenames you choose yourself.


**Pricing:** Goose is free, with no paid plan. You pay your model provider at its own rates.


**Pros:** Free and Apache-2.0, loads GEMINI.md with one setting, both Gemini and Vertex providers


**Cons:** No built-in models, so you always need a key or Vertex, general-purpose rather than coding-only, Google's per-token prices apply in full


**Best fit:** A developer who already pays Google per token and wants a free, open agent around that key.


**Final verdict:** Pick Goose if you'll keep paying Google directly and want one agent for more than code.


### 7. Qwen Code


**Overview:** Qwen Code is the closest relative of Gemini CLI on this list. Its README says it was "originally based on Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2", independent since v0.1, and it keeps the Apache-2.0 license.


Gemini runs through two documented auth types, both on the Gemini protocol: Google GenAI with` GEMINI_API_KEY` , or Vertex AI with a Google API key or keyless Application Default Credentials. The default context file is QWEN.md, so point` context.fileName` at GEMINI.md and your existing file loads.


**Key features:**


- Plan Mode, subagents and git worktrees.
- MCP support and a sandbox.
- Custom providers beside Qwen's own sign-in.


**Pricing:** The software is free, and Gemini on your own key bills at Google's rates. Qwen's own sign-in needs a Plus or Pro subscription priced on chat.qwen.ai, since its free tier ended on April 15, 2026.


**Pros:** Gemini CLI's habits, Apache-2.0, loads GEMINI.md after one setting


**Cons:** Qwen's own sign-in now needs a paid subscription, checkpoints are off by default, no Gemini models without your own key or Vertex


**What feels familiar:** It grew out of Gemini CLI's code, so most of your muscle memory transfers.


**Final verdict:** Choose Qwen Code if you liked Gemini CLI as a tool and only need a new way to pay for Gemini.


### 8. GitHub Copilot CLI


**Overview:** The capture above is the CLI's page, which leads with Copilot as a whole. The CLI comes with every Copilot plan, and apart from Antigravity CLI, it's the only tool here whose docs say it reads GEMINI.md as it is. One quirk is that file references inside GEMINI.md aren't expanded.


Gemini comes from the plan, not your key. Copilot CLI's bring-your-own-key types cover OpenAI-compatible, Azure, Anthropic and Ollama, with no Google type. Pro includes Gemini 3.8 Flash, while Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon need Pro+ at $39 on an individual plan, or Copilot Business at $19 per user. Free users get automatic model selection only.


**Key features:**


- ` /sandbox enable` for local runs and` --cloud` for a cloud sandbox.
- GitHub's own MCP server, plus your own MCP servers.
- Custom instructions from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md as well.


**Pricing:** Copilot Free costs $0 and Pro $10 a month, with Pro+ at $39 and Max at $100. Business costs $19 and Enterprise $39 per user a month.


**Pros:** Reads GEMINI.md as it is, Gemini 3.8 Flash for $10, a cloud sandbox option


**Cons:** For individuals, Gemini 4 needs Pro+ at $39, no own-key route for Gemini, Free can't pick a model, a company-provided seat needs the CLI policy turned on


**The migration upside:** Your GEMINI.md works on day one, and so does a Gemini model on the $10 plan.


**Final verdict:** Choose Copilot CLI if you already pay GitHub and want the move to cost you no file edits.


### 9. Cursor CLI


**Overview:** Cursor CLI runs Cursor's agent from the terminal with the` agent` command, using the same` .cursor/rules` and` mcp.json` as the editor. A Google key setting exists in that editor, but Cursor's docs don't say the CLI uses it.


Gemini sits outside Cursor's included usage. On Premium and above, it runs "at the model's API list price from the first request", and Cursor's page lists $2 per million input tokens for Gemini 4 Argon or Carbon, $10 per million output, and $0.75 and $3.75 for 3.8 Flash. Those are Google's rates before its December 1 and January 1 rises.


**Key features:**


- Plan mode before any edit, cycled with Shift+Tab.
- Git worktrees for parallel runs from the CLI.
- One rules system and MCP config for editor and terminal.


**Pricing:** Cursor's Free plan is limited, Plus costs $8 monthly or $80 a year and runs only Grok and Cursor's Composer models, and Premium costs $30 with four times Plus usage. Super at $100 and Ultra at $200 sit above it, and Gemini bills on top of all three.


**Pros:** The same rules and MCP as Cursor's editor, Gemini on Premium without a Google account of your own, plan mode


**Cons:** Plus runs only Grok and Composer, Gemini billed per token on top of the plan, no GEMINI.md support documented, own-key use not documented for the CLI


**Where it fits:** Teams whose rules already live in Cursor and who want the same agent in a terminal.


**Final verdict:** Pick Cursor CLI if your team already works in Cursor and Gemini is an occasional choice, not your daily model.


### 10. Claude Code


**Overview:** Claude Code is here for readers who are done with Google's models. It runs Claude only, so its answer to the Gemini question is no. The one Google link is that it can run on Google Cloud's Agent Platform, which keeps your Google Cloud bill but still serves Claude.


Your GEMINI.md won't load directly. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md only "when you have no CLAUDE.md in your working directory or above it", so copy your rules into one of those.


**Key features:**


- Plan mode before edits.
- A sandboxed Bash tool you configure.
- MCP servers.


**Pricing:** Claude's Free plan leaves Claude Code out. Pro is $20 billed monthly, dropping to $17 a month on annual billing, and Max at $100 gives five times Pro's usage.


**Pros:** Runs on Google Cloud billing if you need it, plan mode, a sandboxed shell


**Cons:** No Gemini models, not on Claude's free plan, proprietary


**When it makes sense:** When your reason for leaving Gemini CLI is the models, not the tool.


**Final verdict:** Choose Claude Code only if you're ready to drop Gemini altogether.


## Moving your GEMINI.md, extensions and MCP servers


Most of a Gemini CLI setup is plain text, so it moves: your project GEMINI.md, the global` ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` , and MCP server entries in` ~/.gemini/settings.json` . Extensions are the exception, since only Antigravity CLI and Qwen Code document an import for them.


A copy saved as AGENTS.md is worth having too, since OpenCode, Warp and Droid read it by default. In an ICSE 2026 workshop paper, Lulla and colleagues linked an AGENTS.md file to a[28.64% lower median runtime](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20404) and 16.58% lower output token use. That was 10 repositories, 124 pull requests and one agent, and it shows association, not cause.


Context files were still rare in a recent sample. In an MSR 2026 paper, Mohsenimofidi and colleagues scanned 10,000 popular open-source repositories and found that "Only 466 (5%)" had adopted Copilot instructions, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or GEMINI.md, and that[GEMINI.md files were the shortest](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.21413) , at 106 lines on average. A short file is quick to port.


Here's an order that keeps Gemini CLI working while you test the new tool:


1. Copy GEMINI.md to AGENTS.md in the repository root, and keep the original.
2. For Goose, add GEMINI.md to` CONTEXT_FILE_NAMES` ; for Qwen Code, set` context.fileName` ; for OpenCode, list it under` instructions` in` opencode.json` ; in Warp, run` /init` and link it. Copilot CLI and Antigravity CLI need nothing.
3. For Antigravity CLI, accept the config conversion on first launch, then run` agy plugin import gemini` for extensions. Workspace skills live in` .agents/skills/` rather than` .gemini/skills/` .
4. Move MCP servers into the new tool's config. In Antigravity that's` ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` globally or` .agents/mcp_config.json` per workspace, and remote servers'` url` or` httpUrl` key becomes` serverUrl` .
5. Run a real task through old and new tools side by side, and retire Gemini CLI only when the new diff holds up.


If the side-by-side run favors Copilot but its plan prices don't suit you, our[GitHub Copilot alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/github-copilot-alternatives) roundup compares its rivals.


## What Gemini costs per month or per token


You can pay for Gemini through a tool's plan or per token on your own key. Here are the plan routes on this list, cheapest first, with what each price covers.


On your own key, Google's paid tier charges $2 in and $10 out per million tokens for Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon through November 30, 2026, then $4 in and $20 out from December 1. Gemini 3.8 Flash costs $0.75 in and $3.75 out through December 31, 2026, and $1.50 in and $7.50 out from January 1, 2027.


If paying Cursor per token on top of Premium sounds costly, our[Cursor alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/cursor-alternatives) roundup covers editors priced differently.


## How to pick by where you're starting from


Your old Gemini CLI route points to your next tool:


- If you used a free personal account or Google AI Pro, try Antigravity CLI first, since it converts your setup and has a $0 tier.
- If open source matters, pick OpenCode, whose Go plan includes Gemini 4 Argon for $10, or Goose or Qwen Code around your own key.
- If your organization has Code Assist Standard or Enterprise, you can stay for now, but plan the move before annual renewals end on January 31, 2027.
- If you're leaving Google's models entirely, Claude Code is the pick here.


If you'd rather have the agent inside VS Code than in a terminal, our[Cline alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/cline-alternatives) roundup covers editor-based agents.


## Tools we left out


Several more alternatives to Gemini CLI came close. Codex CLI has a built-in Vertex provider, but its docs don't say Gemini models work through it, so its Gemini answer is unclear. Our[Codex alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/codex-alternatives) roundup compares Codex, CLI included, with its rivals.


Crush documents a Gemini key and Vertex, though its license is source-available rather than open source. We excluded Google's new Gemini API CLI, which Gemini CLI's README describes as "not a coding harness", and Gemini Code Assist, which no longer takes new purchases.


## Your first week after Gemini CLI


Move the cheap, reversible parts first. Copy GEMINI.md to AGENTS.md today, run Antigravity CLI's conversion where your Gemini CLI configs live, and give OpenCode Go or Copilot Pro a month before you buy a pricier plan, rechecking Go once its Argon discount ends on November 30.


Some Gemini CLI headless runs are really recurring jobs, such as a weekly report pulled from several apps. Awesomic can run those as[scheduled jobs across your apps](https://www.awesomic.com/apps/use-cases) , so you don't have to keep a cron script alive on your own machine.


## FAQ


### Is Gemini CLI being shut down?


No. It's still open source under Apache 2.0 and still ships releases. Since June 18, 2026, it no longer serves free accounts or Google AI Pro and Ultra, but existing Code Assist Standard and Enterprise organizations and paid Gemini API or Vertex keys still work.


### Is Antigravity CLI free?


At the entry level, yes: the Individual tier costs nothing and covers Gemini 4 Hydrogen and 3.8 Flash under a weekly limit. Gemini 4 Argon needs Google AI Pro, which Google's subscriptions page lists at $19.99 a month.


### Can I still use Gemini CLI with my own API key?


Yes, with a paid Gemini API or Vertex key, which the README now calls "legacy", though Gemini CLI isn't tuned for Gemini 4. Google's pages disagree about unpaid keys, so test yours. On this list, Antigravity CLI, OpenCode, Warp, Factory Droid, Goose and Qwen Code all document a route for your own Gemini key.


### Which Gemini CLI alternatives are open source?


OpenCode is MIT-licensed, Goose and Qwen Code are Apache-2.0 like Gemini CLI, and Warp's client is AGPL v3. Antigravity CLI's and Factory's public repos carry no license, and GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code are proprietary. Cursor publishes no open-source license for its CLI that we found, and Awesomic isn't open source either.


### Can Claude Code run Gemini models?


No. Claude Code runs Claude models only, including when it runs on Google Cloud's Agent Platform. If it's your pick anyway, our[Claude Code alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/claude-code-alternatives) guide compares it with its closest rivals.
